confidence_notes: I used four web searches. The FX figure is the RBA 4pm rate for 18 November 2026 (0.6720 USD per AUD), as shown in search results for the rba.gov.au exchange-rates page. That same day's RBA figures imply roughly 1.10 USD per EUR, which I used to convert euro prices. Restaurant anchors come from crowdsourced averages (Expatica citing Numbeo, June 2026): inexpensive meal about EUR 19, three-course meal for two about EUR 52, draft beer about EUR 3.1, cappuccino about EUR 2.1. I raised the mid-range meal to about EUR 62 because San Sebastian is known for food, restaurant prices run above the Spanish average, and the Numbeo figure looked low. I also nudged coffee and beer up slightly for the July high season. Wine is based on pintxo-bar guides that put a glass of txakoli or wine at about EUR 2.50-4; some of those guides are undated or low quality. I found no reliable cocktail prices, so the cocktail anchor (about EUR 11) is based on its usual price relationship to beer in Spain and is less certain. Accommodation anchors are my own estimates for July peak season, not based on searches or listings. San Sebastian has scarce, expensive summer lodging, so these could be off by plus or minus 25-30%.
comparable_city_reasoning: Restaurant and drink prices are based on San Sebastian's own crowdsourced averages, adjusted with my knowledge of Basque and northern Spanish pricing. Accommodation is based on peak-summer prices in high-demand Spanish coastal and cultural cities such as Barcelona and Bilbao. San Sebastian's July hotel prices are close to Barcelona's and well above Bilbao's.
